finding.text: `review/diff.patch` is stale: the worktree (`C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/qf-6`) has uncommitted changes on top of it — in `Servex/agents/Agents.js`, `Servex/Servex.js`, `Servex/agents/registry.js`, `Servex/agents/awaken-race.test.mjs` — that are not in diff.patch. Their own comments call themselves "fresh-eyes review finding 1/3/4/5/6", so a review already happened and was partly acted on, but never committed or re-exported into the file I was handed. Commit those fixes and regenerate diff.patch before landing; reviewing the stale version below is reviewing code that's already known to be wrong.

`mark_phantom()` (Agents.js, diff.patch's own version, item 2) sets the phantom agent's state to `"idle"`, not `"dormant"`, and never closes its queue. `send()` only calls `awaken()` (which starts a fresh process and replays held turns) when `state === "dormant"` — an `"idle"` agent's `send()` just does `this.queue.push(turn)` straight onto the dead agent's own queue, which nothing is reading any more (the real claude.exe already died). That push still returns `true` (the queue was never `.close()`d), so the message is silently swallowed and the row is marked `"working"` again — the exact failure this whole task exists to close, reintroduced by its own fix. The worktree's uncommitted version already fixes this (state `"dormant"`, queue drained to `held_messages`, `marked_phantom` reset on the next real `awaken()`); that's the version that needs to land, not the one in diff.patch.

`Servex.reconcile()`'s adopt path (diff.patch's version, item 6) calls `this.agents.spawn({ ...row.spec, resume: sid, ... })` to adopt a stray `claude.exe` *before* killing it — for one moment two processes can be resuming the same session id at once. The uncommitted fix in the worktree stops the stray first and only then resumes, which is the safe order the doc comment already claims ("the stray is stopped FIRST"); diff.patch's actual code doesn't do that yet.

Once 1–3 are committed and diff.patch is regenerated, the work itself is solid: I read `requirements.md`'s six build items plus the item 7 addendum one by one against the (fixed) worktree code and each is really there — idle-clock reset in `awaken()` (Agents.js), live-pid cap counting (`working()`), the 60 s starting-stuck requeue and the once-a-minute reconcile (`Servex.reconcile()`, wired from `Global.sweep()`'s existing timer, never a second one), the Inbox fallback in `Heartbeat.post()`/`TaskLoop.escalate()`, `Queue.push()` reporting rejection + `held_messages` replay on awaken, and the `WAIT_REFUSALS` requeue-and-tell-parent-once for both the pool and the OpenRouter pace guard. `node Servex/agents/awaken-race.test.mjs` passes (11 checks) and every existing `Servex/agents/*.test.mjs` / `Servex/*.test.mjs` still passes, run directly in the worktree.

Duplicate `process.kill(pid, 0)` liveness checks (`pid_alive` in Agents.js, `process_alive` in Servex.js, `alive` in registry.js) is exactly what law 6 ("one of everything") warns about — already caught and consolidated to registry.js's `alive()` in the uncommitted fix, just needs committing with the rest.

No simpler way jumps out — six real, independent loss points (a stale idle clock, a cap that trusts a label instead of a process, a start that never begins, nowhere to post an escalation, a queue push nobody checked, and two more spawn-refusal paths that drop silently) plausibly do need six small, separate fixes plus one reconcile sweep; folding them into fewer mechanisms would likely just hide one of them again.

Item 6's reconcile has two halves — the `starting`-stuck requeue (item 3) and the live-process adopt/stop logic (Servex.js, the `claude_processes()` loop in `reconcile()`) — but `awaken-race.test.mjs` only exercises the first half (via `requeue_stuck_start()` directly). The kill-then-adopt path is exactly the kind of code an earlier review round already caught one ordering bug in (the comment at Servex.js's reconcile() cites "fresh-eyes review finding 1"), so it deserves its own direct test before it's trusted unattended.

`WAIT_REFUSALS` (Servex.js, near the bottom) treats the OpenRouter pace guard as transient and requeues it to the head forever, but `evaluate_guard()` (Servex/ext/openrouter/provider.js:273-274) can also fail with "credit left is under $1" — a condition that only clears when the owner tops up the account, not on its own. It won't lose anything (parent is told once, logged once) but it will spin quietly, retrying a dead end every reconcile tick instead of surfacing as a real stop.

The root cause behind requirements.md's item-2 live example — `stop_agent` refusing a long OpenRouter run id with "Bad log name" (Log.js's 64-char check) — is left unfixed on purpose (doc/never-lose-a-wake.md §3: "out of this fix's own fence... not blocking this one"). Reasonable scoping since Log.js isn't in the fence, but `stop_agent` on such an id stays broken until that separate fix happens.

The card proof the brief asks for (test output, item 1's one-line patch verdict, the reconcile's dry-run summary line) isn't in diff.patch, so it can't be checked from this review — worth confirming it actually landed on the card.
